sentences.zh: 馬從聘，字起莘，靈壽人。

translations.literal: Ma Congpin, styled Qishen, was a native of Lingshou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Congpin, whose style was Qishen, came from Lingshou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the seventeenth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授青州推官，擢御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor for Qingzhou, then promoted to remonstrating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor in Qingzhou and later rose to remonstrating censor.

sentences.zh: 勛衛李宗城冊封平秀吉逃歸，從聘言其父言恭不當復督戎政，不從。

translations.literal: When the enfeoffed guardsman Li Zongcheng, who had been sent to invest Ping Xiuji, fled back, Congpin said his father Li Yangong ought not be reappointed to oversee military affairs; the court did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: After the enfeoffed guardsman Li Zongcheng abandoned his mission to invest Hideyoshi and returned home, Congpin argued that Li's father Yangong should not resume command of military affairs; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 出理兩淮鹽課，言近日泰山崩離，坼者裏余，由開礦斷地脈所致，當速罷，不報。

translations.literal: Sent out to administer the Two Huai salt revenue, he said that Mount Tai had recently collapsed and split open for more than a li, caused by mining having severed the earth's pulses, and that mining should be halted at once; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising the Two Huai salt tax, he reported that Mount Tai had lately split apart for more than a li because mining had cut the earth's veins, and urged an immediate halt; the memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 奸人田應璧請掣賣沒官余鹽助大工，帝遣中官魯保督之。

translations.literal: A schemer named Tian Yingbi asked to sell off confiscated surplus salt to fund major works; the emperor sent the eunuch Lu Bao to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: The schemer Tian Yingbi petitioned to liquidate surplus confiscated salt to subsidize great public works, and the emperor dispatched the eunuch Lu Bao to oversee the sale.

sentences.zh: 從聘極陳欺罔狀，不從。

translations.literal: Congpin set forth the fraud in the strongest terms; the court did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: Congpin laid out the deception at length, but again his advice was rejected.

sentences.zh: 還朝，改按浙江，又按蘇、松，請免增蘇、松、常鎮稅課，亦不報。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was reassigned to investigate Zhejiang, then Suzhou and Songjiang, and asked that the added tax levies on Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang be remitted; again no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he was shifted to censorial duty in Zhejiang, then in Suzhou and Songjiang, and petitioned to abolish the newly raised taxes in those prefectures and Zhenjiang; once more there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 以久次擢太仆少卿，拜右僉都御史，巡撫延綏，失事奪俸。

translations.literal: For long service he was promoted Vice Minister of the Stud, then appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Yan-sui; after a military setback his salary was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: After long tenure he was made Vice Minister of the Stud, then Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Yan-sui; a defeat cost him his stipend.

sentences.zh: 既而有搗巢功，未敘，引疾歸。

translations.literal: Later he had merit in raiding enemy nests, but it was not rewarded; he cited illness and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He later won credit for storming rebel strongholds, yet received no promotion for it and retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 加兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 家居凡二十余年，終熹宗世不出。

translations.literal: He remained at home for more than twenty years and never took office again through the entire Chongzhen predecessor's reign.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed home for over twenty years and never served again throughout the Tianqi and Chongzhen reigns of the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十一年冬，大清破靈壽。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year of Chongzhen, the Great Qing broke Lingshou.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Chongzhen 11, the Qing army overran Lingshou.

sentences.zh: 從聘年八十有二矣，謂其三子曰：「吾得死所矣。

translations.literal: Congpin was eighty-two years old and said to his three sons, "I have found the place to die."
translations.idiomatic: At eighty-two Congpin told his three sons, "I have found where I am meant to die."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「吾大臣，義不可生，汝曹生無害也。

translations.literal: He also said, "I am a great minister; by righteousness I cannot live; you may live without harm."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "As a chief minister I am bound by duty not to survive; you may go on living without disgrace."

sentences.zh: 」三子不從。

translations.literal: The three sons would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: His sons refused.

sentences.zh: 從聘縊，三子皆縊。

translations.literal: Congpin hanged himself, and all three sons hanged themselves as well.
translations.idiomatic: Congpin strangled himself, and all three sons did the same.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部尚書，謚介敏，官其一子。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of War, given the posthumous title Jiemin, and one son was granted office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of War with the temple name Jiemin, and one son received an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 耿蔭樓，從聘同邑人也，字旋極。

translations.literal: Geng Yinlou, a fellow townsman of Congpin, styled Xuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Yinlou, from the same county as Congpin, styled Xuanji.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，任臨淄知縣。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign he served as magistrate of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi era he was magistrate of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 久旱，囚服暴烈日中，哭於壇，雨立澍。

translations.literal: During a long drought he wore prisoner's garb and exposed himself in the blazing sun, weeping at the altar, and rain fell at once in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: In a prolonged drought he put on convict dress and stood weeping in the fierce sun at the altar until rain poured down immediately.

sentences.zh: 攝壽光，禱雨如臨淄。

translations.literal: Acting for Shouguang, he prayed for rain as he had at Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: While acting magistrate of Shouguang he prayed for rain with the same result.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，入為兵部主事，調吏部，歷員外郎，乞假歸。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign he entered the Ministry of War as a director, was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, rose through the ranks to vice director, and asked leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he entered the Ministry of War as a director, moved to Personnel, served as vice director, then took leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 城破，偕子參並死之。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he and his son Can died together.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was taken, he and his son Can died together.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 張伯鯨，字繩海，江都人。

translations.literal: Zhang Bojing, styled Shenghai, was a native of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bojing, styled Shenghai, came from Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Wanli 44.

sentences.zh: 歷知會稽、歸安、鄞三縣。

translations.literal: He successively governed the three counties of Kuaiji, Guian, and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as magistrate of Kuaiji, Guian, and Yin.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，大計，調補盧氏。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign, at the grand evaluation, he was transferred to fill the post at Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: At the Tianqi grand evaluation he was reassigned to Lushi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，稍遷戶部主事，出督延、寧二鎮軍儲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was gradually promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue and sent out to supervise military grain stores in the Yan and Ning circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 2 he was promoted to a director in the Ministry of Revenue and sent to oversee army provisions on the Yan and Ning frontiers.

sentences.zh: 自黃甫川西抵寧夏千二百里，不產五谷，芻粟資內地。

translations.literal: From Huangfu west to Ningxia, twelve hundred li produced no grain; fodder and grain depended on the interior.
translations.idiomatic: From Huangfu west to Ningxia, a stretch of twelve hundred li grew no grain and relied on supplies from inland.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭山沿黃河漢、唐二渠，東抵花馬池，素沃野，亦荒蕪甚。

translations.literal: Along the Helan Mountains by the Yellow River were the Han and Tang canals east to Huamachi, once rich fields but now greatly desolate.
translations.idiomatic: The Han and Tang canals along the Yellow River by Helan, east to Huamachi, had been fertile but were now largely waste.

sentences.zh: 伯鯨疏陳其狀，為通商惠工，轉菽麥。

translations.literal: Bojing memorialized the situation, promoting trade and crafts to move beans and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Bojing described the plight in a memorial and urged commerce and crafts to move grain and beans.

sentences.zh: 又仿邊商中鹽意，立官市法以招之，軍民稱便。

translations.literal: He also followed the idea of frontier merchants exchanging salt, establishing government market laws to attract them, and troops and civilians praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He also modeled the frontier salt-exchange system, set up official markets to draw merchants in, and soldiers and civilians alike welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 大盜起延綏，擢伯鯨兵備僉事，轄榆林中路。

translations.literal: When great bandits rose in Yan-sui, Bojing was promoted to military defense vice commissioner, in charge of the middle route at Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: When major banditry broke out in Yan-sui, Bojing was made military defense vice commissioner over the middle route at Yulin.

sentences.zh: 擊破賀思賢，斬一座城、金翅鵬，敗套寇於長樂堡。

translations.literal: He defeated He Sixian, beheaded Yizuocheng and Jinchipeng, and routed the Tatar raiders at Changle Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed He Sixian, killed the bandit chiefs Yizuocheng and Jinchipeng, and routed Tatar raiders at Changle Fort.

sentences.zh: 巡撫陳奇瑜上其功，詔進三階，為右參政，仍視兵備事。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Chen Qiyu reported his merit; an edict advanced him three ranks to Right Vice Commissioner and he still oversaw military defense.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Chen Qiyu reported his victories; the throne advanced him three ranks to Right Vice Commissioner while he retained military defense duties.

sentences.zh: 七年春，奇瑜遷總督，遂擢伯鯨右僉都御史代之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year Qiyu was transferred to grand coordinator, and Bojing was promoted Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 7, when Qiyu became grand coordinator, Bojing was promoted Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 督總兵王承恩等分道擊破插漢部長及套寇於雙山、魚河二堡，斬首三百。

translations.literal: He directed Regional Commander Wang Chengen and others in separate columns to defeat the Chahan chief and Tatar raiders at the twin forts of Shuangshan and Yuhe, beheading three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He directed Regional Commander Wang Chengen and others to rout the Chahan chief and Tatar raiders at Shuangshan and Yuhe forts, taking three hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 明年，以拾遺論罷。

translations.literal: The next year he was dismissed on a remonstrance memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was removed after a remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 尋論延綏功，詔起用，蔭子錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: Soon afterward his Yan-sui service was recognized; an edict recalled him and enfeoffed his son as a thousand-household guardsman in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his Yan-sui achievements were recognized; he was recalled by edict and his son enfeoffed as an Embroidered-Uniform Guard chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 十年秋，楊嗣昌議大舉討賊，遣戶部一侍郎駐池州，專理兵食。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the tenth year Yang Sichang planned a major campaign against the rebels and sent one vice minister of Revenue to station at Chizhou solely to manage army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of year 10 Yang Sichang planned a great pacification drive and stationed a Revenue vice minister at Chizhou to handle army grain alone.

sentences.zh: 帝命傅淑訓。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Fu Shuxun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Fu Shuxun.

sentences.zh: 明年，淑訓憂去，即家起伯鯨代之，如淑訓官。

translations.literal: The next year Shuxun left on mourning; Bojing was summoned from home to replace him with the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shuxun left for mourning and Bojing was called from home to replace him at the same rank.

sentences.zh: 又明年，熊文燦撫事敗，嗣昌自出督師，移伯鯨襄陽。

translations.literal: The year after, when Xiong Wencan's pacification failed, Sichang took command in person and moved Bojing to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The year after, when Xiong Wencan's pacification collapsed, Sichang took the field himself and shifted Bojing to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 文燦之被逮也，言剿餉不至者六十余萬，伯鯨坐貶秩。

translations.literal: When Wencan was arrested he said more than six hundred thousand taels of pacification funds had not arrived; Bojing was demoted in rank for this.
translations.idiomatic: At Wencan's arrest he claimed over six hundred thousand taels of pacification funds had never arrived; Bojing was demoted for the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 十五年，召為兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was summoned as Left Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he was recalled as Left Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年，尚書馮元飆在告，伯鯨攝部事。

translations.literal: The next year Minister Feng Yuanbiao was on leave and Bojing acted as head of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, with Minister Feng Yuanbiao on leave, Bojing acted as head of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 召對萬歲山，疾作，中官扶出，遂乞休。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience at Wansuishan, he fell ill; eunuchs helped him out and he then asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience at Wansuishan he fell ill, was helped out by eunuchs, and petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 又明年，京城陷，微服遁還。

translations.literal: The year after, when the capital fell, he slipped away in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the capital fell, he fled home in disguise.

sentences.zh: 福王立於南京，伯鯨家居不出。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing; Bojing stayed home and did not come forth.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing, Bojing remained at home.

sentences.zh: 久之，揚州被圍，與當事分城守。

translations.literal: After a long while Yangzhou was besieged; he joined the authorities in dividing the city for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Yangzhou came under siege; he joined the officials in dividing the walls for defense.

sentences.zh: 城破，自經死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was lost he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 宋玫，字文玉，萊陽人。

translations.literal: Song Mei, styled Wenyu, was a native of Laiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Song Mei, styled Wenyu, was from Laiyang.

sentences.zh: 父繼登，萬歷三十二年進士。

translations.literal: His father Jideng passed the jinshi in the thirty-second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jideng had been a jinshi in Wanli 32.

sentences.zh: 歷官陜西右參議。

translations.literal: He had served as Right Vice Commissioner in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen to Right Vice Commissioner in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年大計謫官。

translations.literal: At the grand evaluation of the fifth year of Tianqi he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: At the Tianqi 5 grand evaluation he was cashiered.

sentences.zh: 玫即以是年偕族叔應亨同舉進士，玫授虞城知縣，應亨得清豐。

translations.literal: Mei in that same year passed the jinshi together with his clansman Yingheng; Mei was made magistrate of Yucheng and Yingheng received Qingfeng.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Mei and his clansman Yingheng both passed the jinshi; Mei was sent to Yucheng and Yingheng to Qingfeng.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，玫兄琮亦舉進士，知祥符，而玫以才調繁杞縣，三人壤地相接，並有治聲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen Mei's elder brother Cong also passed the jinshi and governed Xiangfu, while Mei for talent was transferred to the demanding county of Qi; the three men's jurisdictions bordered one another and all won praise for good government.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 Mei's brother Cong also became a jinshi and governed Xiangfu, while Mei was moved to busy Qi County for his ability; their districts adjoined and all three were famed for good rule.

sentences.zh: 應亨遷禮部主事，玫亦擢吏科給事中。

translations.literal: Yingheng was moved to the Ministry of Rites as a director, and Mei was promoted remonstrating censor in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Yingheng entered the Ministry of Rites as a director and Mei was made a remonstrating censor in Personnel.

sentences.zh: 嘗疏論用人，謂：「陛下求治之心愈急，則浮薄喜事之人皆飾詭而釣奇；

translations.literal: He once memorialized on appointments, saying: "The more urgently Your Majesty seeks good government, the more shallow men eager for novelty dress up deceit to fish for marvels;"
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized on appointments, saying, "The more urgently Your Majesty seeks order, the more shallow opportunists dress up trickery to court wonder;"

sentences.zh: 陛下破格之意愈殷，則巧言孔壬之徒皆乘機而鬥捷。

translations.literal: "the more generously Your Majesty breaks precedent, the more glib villains seize the moment to compete for favor."
translations.idiomatic: "and the more freely Your Majesty breaks precedent, the more smooth talkers rush in to win favor."

sentences.zh: 」眾韙其言。

translations.literal: The crowd approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Many applauded the point.

sentences.zh: 時應亨已改吏部，累遷稽勛郎中，落職歸。

translations.literal: At that time Yingheng had already moved to Personnel, risen through the ranks to director in the Merit Office, and left office to return home.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yingheng had moved to Personnel, risen to director in the Merit Office, and gone home after dismissal.

sentences.zh: 玫方除母喪，起故官，歷刑科都給事中。

translations.literal: Mei had just finished mourning for his mother, resumed his former post, and rose through remonstrating censor in the Ministry of Punishments to chief remonstrating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Mei had just left mourning, resumed office, and advanced to chief remonstrating censor in Punishments.

sentences.zh: 請熱審概行於天下。

translations.literal: He asked that the summer judicial review be applied throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that the summer judicial review be extended empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 又言獄囚稽滯瘐死，與刑死幾相半，宜有矜釋。

translations.literal: He also said prisoners long detained died of illness in numbers nearly equal to executions, and that mercy releases were fitting.
translations.idiomatic: He also said prisoners held so long they died of neglect nearly matched those executed, and should be released on mercy.

sentences.zh: 帝采納之。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted both proposals.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿，歷大理卿、工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was moved to Vice Minister of Ceremonies, then served as President of the Court of Judicial Review and Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Minister of Ceremonies, then President of the Court of Judicial Review and Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 玫父繼登已久廢，至是為浙江右參政。

translations.literal: Mei's father Jideng had long been out of office; now he was made Right Vice Commissioner in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Mei's father Jideng, long out of office, was now made Right Vice Commissioner in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 大學士周延儒客盛順者，為浙江巡撫熊奮渭營內召，果擢南京戶部侍郎，繼登父子信之。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru's client Sheng Shun had the Zhejiang grand coordinator Xiong Fenwei lobby for his recall to court; he was indeed made Nanjing Vice Minister of Revenue, and the Jideng father and son believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru's client Sheng Shun had Zhejiang Grand Coordinator Xiong Fenwei lobby for his recall; he was made Nanjing Vice Minister of Revenue, and the Jidengs took it as proof of favor.

sentences.zh: 十五年夏，廷推閣臣，順為玫營推甚力。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifteenth year, when the court nominated grand secretaries, Shun campaigned vigorously to have Mei nominated.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of year 15, during court nomination of grand secretaries, Shun pushed hard for Mei.

sentences.zh: 會詔令再推，玫與焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a second round of nominations and Mei was included.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called for a second nomination round and Mei was on the list.

sentences.zh: 帝已中流言，疑諸臣有私。

translations.literal: The emperor had already been swayed by rumors and suspected the ministers of private dealing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, already swayed by rumor, suspected collusion.

sentences.zh: 比入對，玫冀得帝意，侃侃敷奏。

translations.literal: When Mei came to audience he hoped to win the emperor's favor and spoke at length with confidence.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Mei hoped to please him and spoke boldly at length.

sentences.zh: 帝發怒，叱退之，與吏部尚書李日宣等並下獄。

translations.literal: The emperor flew into a rage, shouted him down, and imprisoned him together with Minister of Personnel Li Rixuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor erupted, drove him out, and jailed him with Minister of Personnel Li Rixuan and others.

sentences.zh: 日宣等遣戍，玫除名，順乃驚竄。

translations.literal: Rixuan and the rest were banished; Mei was struck from the rolls, and Shun fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Rixuan and others were exiled; Mei was removed from office and Shun fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 閏十一月，臨清破，應亨與知縣陳顯際謀城守。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month Linqing fell; Yingheng and Magistrate Chen Xianji planned to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month, when Linqing fell, Yingheng and Magistrate Chen Xianji resolved to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 應亨以城北庳薄，出千金建甕城，浹旬而畢。

translations.literal: Yingheng, finding the north wall low and thin, spent a thousand taels to build a barbican wall, finished in ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Yingheng, seeing the north wall weak, spent a thousand taels on a barbican finished in ten days.

sentences.zh: 玫及邑人趙士驥亦出貲治守具。

translations.literal: Mei and the townsman Zhao Shiji also contributed funds for defense equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Mei and the townsman Zhao Shiji also paid for defensive gear.

sentences.zh: 無何，大清兵薄城，城上火炮矢石並發，圍乃解。

translations.literal: Before long Qing troops pressed the city; cannon, fire-arrows, and stones rained from the walls and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qing forces closed in; cannon, arrows, and stones poured from the walls and the siege lifted.

sentences.zh: 明年二月復至，城遂破，玫、應亨、顯際、士驥並死之。

translations.literal: The next year in the second month they returned; the city fell and Mei, Yingheng, Xianji, and Shiji all died.
translations.idiomatic: They returned the second month of the following year; the city fell and Mei, Yingheng, Xianji, and Shiji all perished.

sentences.zh: 顯際，真定人，士驥官中書舍人，並起家進士。

translations.literal: Xianji was from Zhending; Shiji held the post of Secretariat drafter; both had begun as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Xianji was from Zhending; Shiji was a Secretariat drafter; both were jinshi.

sentences.zh: 玫、應亨有文名。

translations.literal: Mei and Yingheng had literary reputations.
translations.idiomatic: Mei and Yingheng were known for their writing.

sentences.zh: 沈迅，亦萊陽人也。

translations.literal: Shen Xun was also from Laiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xun, too, was from Laiyang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年舉進士，歷知新城、蠡二縣，與膠州張若麒同年友善。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he passed the jinshi examination, successively governed Xincheng and Li counties, and was on friendly terms with his fellow graduate Zhang Ruoqi of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Chongzhen 4, served as magistrate of Xincheng and Li, and was close friends with his classmate Zhang Ruoqi of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 十一年行取入都。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was selected by special promotion and entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he was promoted by special selection to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝以吏部考選行私，親策諸臣，迅、若騏並得刑部主事。

translations.literal: Because the Ministry of Personnel's evaluation showed favoritism, the emperor personally examined the candidates; Xun and Ruoqi both received posts as directors in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor found the Personnel evaluation corrupt, he examined candidates himself; Xun and Ruoqi were both made directors in Punishments.

sentences.zh: 兩人大恚恨，結楊嗣昌，得改兵部。

translations.literal: The two men were greatly resentful, attached themselves to Yang Sichang, and were transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter over the outcome, they allied with Yang Sichang and won transfer to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，畿輔被兵，迅請於廣平、河間、定州、蠡縣各設兵備一人。

translations.literal: That winter the capital region suffered warfare; Xun asked that one military defense commissioner be appointed each for Guangping, Hejian, Dingzhou, and Li County.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital region came under attack that winter, he urged appointing a military defense commissioner for each of Guangping, Hejian, Dingzhou, and Li.

sentences.zh: 又請以天下僧人配尼姑，編入裏甲，三丁抽一，可得兵數十萬。

translations.literal: He also asked that Buddhist monks throughout the empire be paired with nuns, registered in neighborhood tithing units, and one man taken from every three households, yielding several hundred thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed registering monks with nuns in local militia rolls and drafting one man in three, claiming this would yield hundreds of thousands of soldiers.

sentences.zh: 他條奏甚多。

translations.literal: His other memorial clauses were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted many other proposals besides.

sentences.zh: 章下兵部，嗣昌盛稱迅言可用，乃命為兵科給事中。

translations.literal: The memorial went to the Ministry of War; Sichang praised Xun's words as useful, and he was appointed remonstrating censor in the War Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The War Ministry received his papers; Sichang praised them and Xun was made a remonstrating censor in the War Bureau.

sentences.zh: 迅欲自結於帝，數言事，皆中旨。

translations.literal: Xun wished to win the emperor's favor, spoke on affairs repeatedly, and all hit the mark with the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking favor with the throne, he spoke often on policy and usually pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 當是時，軍興方棘，廷臣言兵者即以為知兵，大者推督撫，小者兵備，一當事任，罪累立至。

translations.literal: At that time military campaigns were pressing; any courtier who spoke of war was deemed to know war—grand coordinators for the great, military defense commissioners for the small—and once one took office, blame piled up at once.
translations.idiomatic: With war urgent, any official who talked of armies was treated as an expert; grand coordinators and defense commissioners alike were blamed the moment they took post.

sentences.zh: 於是上下諱言兵，章奏無敢及者。

translations.literal: Thereupon above and below they shunned speaking of war, and no memorial dared touch it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon everyone avoided discussing military affairs in memorials.

sentences.zh: 迅極言其弊，乞敕廷臣五日內陳方略。

translations.literal: Xun spoke forcefully of the evil of this and begged an edict that within five days the court ministers set forth strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Xun denounced the taboo and asked the emperor to order ministers to present strategy within five days.

sentences.zh: 帝即從其言。

translations.literal: The emperor at once followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed immediately.

sentences.zh: 迅考選時為掌河南道御史王萬象所抑，因事劾罷萬象，勢益張，與若麒盡把持山東事。

translations.literal: At his evaluation Xun had been suppressed by the censor in charge of the Henan circuit Wang Wanxiang; he impeached and removed Wanxiang on a pretext, grew more overbearing, and with Ruoqi monopolized Shandong affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Passed over in evaluation by Henan circuit censor Wang Wanxiang, he impeached and ousted him, grew bolder, and with Ruoqi dominated Shandong affairs.

sentences.zh: 會順天府丞戴澳誣劾平遠知縣王凝命、嘉興推官文德翼貪，迅上疏頌二人廉能，澳下吏削籍。

translations.literal: When Shuntian vice prefect Dai Ao falsely impeached Pingyuan Magistrate Wang Ningming and Jiaxing investigating censor Wen Deyi for graft, Xun memorialized praising the two men's integrity and ability; Ao was handed to the law officers and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuntian vice prefect Dai Ao falsely accused Pingyuan magistrate Wang Ningming and Jiaxing investigating censor Wen Deyi of corruption, Xun praised their integrity; Ao was arrested and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 迅累遷禮科都給事中。

translations.literal: Xun was repeatedly promoted to chief remonstrating censor in the Rites Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief remonstrating censor in the Rites Bureau.

sentences.zh: 陳新甲主款，迅面斥其非，廷辨良久，又言：「楊嗣昌死有余戮，借久案以邀功，陳新甲負罪不遑，移邊勞而錄蔭，非論功議罪法。

translations.literal: Chen Xinjia favored peace talks; Xun rebuked him to his face in court debate for a long time, and also said: "Yang Sichang deserved death many times over; he used an old case to seek merit. Chen Xinjia, guilty and in flight, shifted border labor into enfeoffment records—this is not the law for weighing merit and assigning guilt."
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xinjia pushed peace talks, Xun denounced him in open court debate, saying Yang Sichang deserved execution many times over for trading on an old case, while Xinjia, fleeing guilt, turned border service into hereditary honors—neither was proper merit law.

sentences.zh: 」帝是其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with him.

sentences.zh: 迅本由嗣昌進，隨眾詆毀，時論訾薄之。

translations.literal: Xun had originally advanced through Sichang; he followed the crowd in reviling him, and opinion despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Though Sichang had promoted him, he joined the chorus against Sichang, and contemporaries scorned him for it.

sentences.zh: 尋以保舉高鬥光為鳳陽總督不當，謫國子博士，乞假歸。

translations.literal: Soon he was demoted to National University lecturer for improperly recommending Gao Douguang as Fengyang grand coordinator, and asked leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon demoted to National University lecturer for a bad recommendation of Gao Douguang as Fengyang grand coordinator, then went home on leave.

sentences.zh: 及新甲誅，命追論兵科不糾發罪，吏部上迅名。

translations.literal: When Xinjia was executed, an order was issued to review the War Bureau's failure to expose the crime; the Ministry of Personnel submitted Xun's name.
translations.idiomatic: After Xinjia's execution the court reviewed the War Bureau's failure to expose his crimes, and Personnel listed Xun.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「迅御前駁議，朕猶識之，可復故官。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Xun's rebuttal before the throne—I still remember it; he may resume his former post."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I still remember Xun debating before me; restore his former post."

sentences.zh: 」未赴而京師陷。

translations.literal: Before he could take up office the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet returned when the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 迅家居，與弟迓設砦自衛。

translations.literal: Xun stayed home and with his younger brother Ya built a stockade for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: At home he and his brother Ya built a fortified camp.

sentences.zh: 迓短小精悍，馬上舞百斤鐵椎。

translations.literal: Ya was short, keen, and on horseback could swing a hundred-jin iron mace.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was small but fierce and could whirl a hundred-jin iron mace on horseback.

sentences.zh: 兄弟率里中壯士，捕剿土寇略盡。

translations.literal: The brothers led stalwart men of the neighborhood and hunted down local bandits until few remained.
translations.idiomatic: They led local braves and nearly wiped out bandits in the area.

sentences.zh: 大清兵至，破砦，迅闔門死之。

translations.literal: When Qing troops arrived they broke the stockade; Xun and his whole household died.
translations.idiomatic: Qing forces overran the camp; Xun and his entire household perished.

sentences.zh: 若麒劾黃道周以媚嗣昌。

translations.literal: Ruoqi impeached Huang Daozhou to please Sichang.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoqi impeached Huang Daozhou to curry favor with Sichang.

sentences.zh: 歷職方郎中，新甲遣赴寧、錦督戰，覆洪承疇等十余萬軍，獨渡海逃還，論死系獄。

translations.literal: He served as director in the Bureau of Appointments; Xinjia sent him to supervise war at Ning and Jin, where Hong Chengchou and more than a hundred thousand troops were destroyed; he alone fled back across the sea, was sentenced to death, and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: As Appointments director he was sent by Xinjia to Ning-Jin, where Hong Chengchou's army of over one hundred thousand was ruined; he alone escaped by sea, was condemned to death, and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷都城，出降。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng took the capital he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng seized the capital he submitted.

sentences.zh: 吏部張捷薦逆黨呂純如，淑泰極論其謬，並論大學士王應熊朋比行私，劾捷徇應熊意，用其私人王維章撫蜀。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zhang Jie recommended the rebel partisan Lu Chunru; Shutai argued strongly against the error, and also attacked Grand Secretary Wang Yingxiong for factional favoritism, impeaching Jie for following Yingxiong's wishes in appointing his private man Wang Weizhang to pacify Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel Minister Zhang Jie recommended the eunuch partisan Lu Chunru; Shutai denounced the appointment and accused Grand Secretary Wang Yingxiong of clique favoritism, charging Jie with placing his client Wang Weizhang in Sichuan at Yingxiong's bidding.

sentences.zh: 言：「維章官西寧，坐加征激變，落職閑住。

translations.literal: He said, "Weizhang governed Xining, was dismissed for provoking rebellion through excessive levies, and lives in retirement."
translations.idiomatic: He said Weizhang had governed Xining, been removed after levies sparked mutiny, and now lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 捷朦朧啟事，明肆奸欺。

translations.literal: Jie reported the matter vaguely, plainly practicing deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Jie filed a vague report, openly practicing fraud.

sentences.zh: 」帝責捷自陳。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jie to explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jie to explain.

sentences.zh: 捷詆淑泰黨同伐異，帝不問。

translations.literal: Jie slandered Shutai for partisan attack; the emperor did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: Jie accused Shutai of factional attack; the emperor ignored it.

sentences.zh: 時皇陵被毀，巡撫楊一鵬得罪。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial tombs were destroyed and Grand Coordinator Yang Yipeng was blamed.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial tombs were ravaged, Grand Coordinator Yang Yipeng was blamed.

sentences.zh: 應熊以座主故，力庇之。

translations.literal: Yingxiong, as his examination patron, shielded him with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiong, as Yipeng's patron, shielded him fiercely.

sentences.zh: 淑泰發其停匿章奏狀，帝亦不究。

translations.literal: Shutai exposed his withholding of memorials, but the emperor also did not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Shutai exposed his suppression of memorials, but the emperor did not investigate.

sentences.zh: 淑泰乃摭應熊納賄數事上之，應熊捐貲助陵工，淑泰又劾其召寇庇奸。

translations.literal: Shutai then gathered several matters of Yingxiong's bribe-taking and submitted them; Yingxiong donated funds for tomb repair, and Shutai again impeached him for inviting bandits and shielding villains.
translations.idiomatic: Shutai then listed Yingxiong's bribes; Yingxiong donated to tomb repairs, and Shutai impeached him again for harboring traitors.

sentences.zh: 帝責以挾私求勝，終不納。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for seeking victory through private spite, and in the end did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused him of private spite and rejected the charges.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，上疏言：「今以措餉故，至搜括借助。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year he memorialized, saying: "Now for raising funds they have gone so far as forced exactions and borrowing."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year 11 he wrote, "To raise funds the court now resorts to forced levies and borrowing."

sentences.zh: 即行之而得，再有兵事，能復行乎！

translations.literal: Even if these are carried out and succeed, when war comes again can they be carried out again?
translations.idiomatic: Even if they work once, how can they be repeated when war returns?

sentences.zh: 治不規其可久，徒倉皇於補救之術，非所以為忠也。

translations.literal: To govern without planning for what can last, but only rush about with remedies, is not how to show loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Governing without durable plans and only patching in haste is not loyal service.

sentences.zh: 陛下方以清節風天下，而乃條敘百官金錢於多寡之間，是教之貪也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just now using integrity to inspire the empire, yet you list officials' money by greater and lesser amounts—this teaches greed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty seeks to inspire integrity, yet ranking officials' wealth teaches greed.

sentences.zh: 至借貸之說，尤不可行。

translations.literal: As for the proposal to borrow, it especially cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The borrowing scheme above all must be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 京師根本重地，邇者物力困竭，富商大賈大半旋歸。

translations.literal: The capital is the empire's root; lately material strength is exhausted and great merchants have mostly gone home.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing is the empire's foundation; goods are exhausted and wealthy merchants have fled.

sentences.zh: 內不安，何以攘外！

translations.literal: If the interior is unsettled, how can the exterior be secured!
translations.idiomatic: With the interior unsettled, how can we face outward threats?

sentences.zh: 乞立寢其說。

translations.literal: I beg that this proposal be halted at once.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to abandon it immediately.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「強兵莫如行法。

translations.literal: He also said, "To strengthen troops nothing surpasses enforcing the law."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Strong armies require strict law."

sentences.zh: 今之兵，索餉則強，赴敵則弱；

translations.literal: Today's troops are strong in demanding pay and weak in facing the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Today's soldiers bully for pay but flee the enemy;

sentences.zh: 殺良冒功則強，除暴救民則弱。

translations.literal: strong in killing the innocent to claim merit, weak in suppressing violence and saving the people.
translations.idiomatic: bold in killing civilians for credit, timid in protecting the people.

sentences.zh: 請明示法令，諸將能用命殺賊者，立擢為大將，否則死無赦。

translations.literal: I ask that the laws be made clear: any commander who can obey orders and kill bandits shall be promoted at once to grand general, otherwise death without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Make the law plain: commanders who obey and kill rebels rise to grand general; those who fail die without mercy.

sentences.zh: 毋以降級戴罪，徒為不切身之痛癢。

translations.literal: Do not use demotion and bearing guilt as punishments that are only pain and itch unrelated to the person.
translations.idiomatic: Do not treat demotion as a painless slap on the wrist.

sentences.zh: 」帝是其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十五年遷吏科，典浙江鄉試，事竣還家。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was moved to the Personnel Bureau, conducted the Zhejiang provincial examination, and when finished returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he entered the Personnel Bureau, ran the Zhejiang provincial exams, then went home.

sentences.zh: 十二月，大清兵圍兗州，淑泰竭力固守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Qing troops besieged Yanzhou; Shutai defended with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Qing forces besieged Yanzhou and Shutai defended fiercely.

sentences.zh: 城破，死之。

translations.literal: When the city fell he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he died.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太仆少卿，官一子。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Vice Minister of the Stud and granted office to one son.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Stud and one son received office.

sentences.zh: 高名衡，字仲平，沂州人。

translations.literal: Gao Mingheng, styled Zhongping, was a native of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mingheng, styled Zhongping, came from Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Chongzhen 4.

sentences.zh: 除如臯知縣，以才調興化，征授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Rugao; for talent he was transferred to Xinghua, then summoned and made censor.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Rugao, was transferred to Xinghua for ability, then summoned as censor.

sentences.zh: 十二年出按河南。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he went out to investigate Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was sent to inspect Henan.

sentences.zh: 明年期滿，留再巡一年。

translations.literal: The next year when his term ended he was kept for another year of inspection.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was kept another year.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，李自成陷洛陽，乘勝遂圍開封。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year Li Zicheng took Luoyang and pressed on to besiege Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 14 Li Zicheng took Luoyang and besieged Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 巡撫李仙風時在河北，名衡集眾守。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Li Xianfeng was then in Hebei; Mingheng gathered the people to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Li Xianfeng was in Hebei; Mingheng rallied the defense.

sentences.zh: 周王恭枵發庫金百萬兩，募死士殺賊，烝米屑麥，執爨以餉軍，凡七晝夜。

translations.literal: Prince Gong of Zhou Xu opened the treasury for a million taels, recruited dare-to-die men to kill bandits, steamed rice and ground wheat, personally cooked to feed the army—for seven days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong Xu spent a million taels from the treasury, recruited volunteers, ground grain and cooked for the troops for seven days and nights.

sentences.zh: 仙風馳還開封，副將陳永福背城而戰，斬首二千。

translations.literal: Xianfeng raced back to Kaifeng; Vice General Chen Yongfu fought with his back to the wall and beheaded two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfeng rushed back; Vice General Chen Yongfu fought with the wall at his back and took two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 遊擊高謙夾擊，斬首七百。

translations.literal: Roving-brigade commander Gao Qian struck from both sides and beheaded seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Roving commander Gao Qian attacked from both flanks and took seven hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 賊解去。

translations.literal: The bandits lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 仙風既還，與名衡互訐奏。

translations.literal: After Xianfeng returned, he and Mingheng impeached each other in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Once back, Xianfeng and Mingheng traded impeachment memorials.

sentences.zh: 帝以陷福藩罪詔逮仙風，以襄陽兵備副使張克儉代。

translations.literal: The emperor, blaming the fall of the Prince of Fu's domain, ordered Xianfeng arrested and replaced him with Yan-Yang military defense vice commissioner Zhang Kejian.
translations.idiomatic: Blaming the loss of the Fu prince's domain, the emperor arrested Xianfeng and named Zhang Kejian to replace him.

sentences.zh: 克儉已前死難，即擢名衡右僉都御史代之。

translations.literal: Kejian had already died in battle earlier; Mingheng was at once promoted Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian had already died in battle; Mingheng was promoted Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 以永福充總兵官都督僉事，鎮守河南。

translations.literal: Yongfu was made regional commander and Vice Commissioner-in-Chief to guard Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yongfu was made regional commander and Vice Commissioner-in-Chief defending Henan.

sentences.zh: 當是時，賊連陷南陽、鄧、汝十余州縣，唐、徽二王遇害，名稀不能救。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits successively took Nanyang, Deng, Ru, and more than ten prefectures and counties; the Princes of Tang and Hui were killed; Mingheng could not save them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits then seized Nanyang, Deng, Ru, and a dozen counties; the Tang and Hui princes were killed and Mingheng could not rescue them.

sentences.zh: 開封周邸圖書文物之盛甲他藩，士大夫垔富，蓄積充刃。

translations.literal: The Zhou mansion at Kaifeng had books and relics surpassing other princely houses; scholar-officials were wealthy and stores overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng's Zhou palace held finer collections than other princes; officials were rich and stores abundant.

sentences.zh: 自成攻之不能克，然欲得而甘心焉。

translations.literal: Zicheng could not take it by assault, yet wished to possess it to his heart's content.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng could not storm it but was determined to have it.

sentences.zh: 十二月杪，賊再圍開封。

translations.literal: At the end of the twelfth month the bandits besieged Kaifeng again.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end they besieged Kaifeng again.

sentences.zh: 永福射自成，中其左目，炮殪上天龍等。

translations.literal: Yongfu shot Zicheng and hit his left eye; cannon killed Shang Tianlong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yongfu shot Zicheng in the left eye; cannon killed Shang Tianlong and others.

sentences.zh: 自成大怒，急攻之。

translations.literal: Zicheng was furious and pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Zicheng pressed the assault.

sentences.zh: 開封故宋汴都，金帝南遷所重築也，厚數丈，內堅致而疏外。

translations.literal: Kaifeng was the old Song capital of Bian, rebuilt when the Jin emperor moved south; the walls were several zhang thick, hard within and loose without.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng, old Song Bianliang, had been rebuilt thick and hard inside, softer outside.

sentences.zh: 賊用火藥放迸，火發即外擊，<番瓦>瓳飛鳴，賊騎皆糜爛，自成大驚。

translations.literal: The bandits used gunpowder to blast; when the fire burst outward, bricks and tiles screamed through the air, and the bandit horsemen were all pulverized; Zicheng was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: They blasted the walls with gunpowder; the blast hurled bricks outward, shattering rebel cavalry and startling Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 會楊文嶽援兵亦至，乃解圍去。

translations.literal: When Yang Wenyue's relief army also arrived, they lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wenyue's relief arrived and the siege lifted.

sentences.zh: 西華、郾、襄、睢、陳、太康、商丘、寧陵、考城俱陷。

translations.literal: Xihua, Yan, Xiang, Sui, Chen, Taikang, Shangqiu, Ningling, and Kaocheng all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Xihua, Yan, Xiang, Sui, Chen, Taikang, Shangqiu, Ningling, and Kaocheng all fell.

sentences.zh: 十五年四月復至開封，圍而不攻，欲坐困之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year they came again to Kaifeng, besieging without assault, intending to wear it down.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 15 they returned, besieging without assault to starve the city.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝詔釋故尚書侯恂於獄，命督保定、山東、河北、湖北諸軍務，並轄平賊等鎮援剿官兵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the emperor ordered the former minister Hou Xun released from prison to supervise military affairs in Baoding, Shandong, Hebei, and Hubei, and also command the pacification garrisons and relief armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor freed former minister Hou Xun to command armies in Baoding, Shandong, Hebei, and Hubei and the pacification forces.

sentences.zh: 拔知縣蘇京、王漢、王燮為御史。

translations.literal: Magistrates Su Jing, Wang Han, and Wang Xie were elevated to censors.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates Su Jing, Wang Han, and Wang Xie were made censors.

sentences.zh: 詔蘇京監延、寧、甘、固軍，趣孫傳庭出關；

translations.literal: An edict ordered Su Jing to supervise the Yan, Ning, Gan, and Gu armies and urge Sun Chuan ting to march out;
translations.idiomatic: Su Jing was ordered to oversee Yan, Ning, Gan, and Gu troops and hurry Sun Chuanting out of the passes;

sentences.zh: 王漢監平賊鎮標楚、蜀軍，同侯恂等急擊；

translations.literal: Wang Han to supervise the Chu and Shu troops of the Pacification Army and strike urgently with Hou Xun;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han to lead Pacification Army Chu and Shu troops with Hou Xun;

sentences.zh: 王燮監陽、懷東晉軍，刻期渡河。

translations.literal: and Wang Xie to supervise the Yang and Huai eastern Jin armies, with a fixed date to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: and Wang Xie to lead Yang and Huai eastern Jin forces across the river on schedule.

sentences.zh: 總兵許定國以晉軍次沁水，一夕潰去，寧武兵亦潰於懷慶，詔逮定國。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Xu Dingguo camped the Jin army at Qinshui; in one night it dispersed; Ningwu troops also broke at Huaqing; an edict arrested Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Xu Dingguo's Jin army camped at Qinshui and fled overnight; Ningwu troops broke at Huaqing; Dingguo was arrested.

sentences.zh: 七月，河上之兵潰。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the armies on the river collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the river armies collapsed.

sentences.zh: 督師丁啟睿、保督楊文嶽合左良玉、虎大威、楊德政、方國安諸軍，次於朱仙鎮。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Ding Qirui and Pacification Commissioner Yang Wenyue combined the armies of Zuo Liangyu, Hu Dawei, Yang Dezheng, and Fang Guo'an and camped at Zhuxian Town.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Qirui and Yang Wenyue gathered Zuo Liangyu, Hu Dawei, Yang Dezheng, and Fang Guo'an at Zhuxian Town.

sentences.zh: 良玉走還襄陽，諸軍皆潰，啟睿、文嶽奔汝寧。

translations.literal: Liangyu fled back to Xiangyang; all armies broke; Qirui and Wenyue ran to Runing.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu fled to Xiangyang; the armies scattered; Qirui and Wenyue fled to Runing.

sentences.zh: 詔山東總兵官劉澤清援開封。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shandong regional commander Liu Zeqing to relieve Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong regional commander Liu Zeqing was ordered to relieve Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 城中食盡，名衡、永福偕監司梁炳、蘇壯、吳士講，同知蘇茂灼，通判彭士奇，推官黃澍等守益堅。

translations.literal: Food in the city was exhausted; Mingheng and Yongfu with supervisors Liang Bing, Su Zhuang, and Wu Shijiang, vice prefect Su Maozhuo, transit commissioner Peng Shiji, and investigating censor Huang Shu and others defended ever more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: When food ran out, Mingheng, Yongfu, Liang Bing, Su Zhuang, Wu Shijiang, Su Maozhuo, Peng Shiji, Huang Shu, and others held ever firmer.

sentences.zh: 澤清以兵來援，諸軍並集河北朱家寨不敢進。

translations.literal: Zeqing came with troops in relief; all armies gathered at Zhujiazhai north of the river but dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zeqing arrived, but allied armies camped at Zhujiazhai north of the river and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 澤清曰：「朱家寨去開封八里。

translations.literal: Zeqing said, "Zhujiazhai is eight li from Kaifeng."
translations.idiomatic: Zeqing said, "Zhujiazhai is eight li from Kaifeng."

sentences.zh: 我以兵五千南渡，依河而營，引水環之。

translations.literal: I will cross south with five thousand men, camp along the river, and draw water to ring the camp.
translations.idiomatic: I will cross with five thousand men, camp on the riverbank, and ring the camp with water.

sentences.zh: 以次結八營，直達大堤。

translations.literal: In succession I will build eight camps reaching the great dike.
translations.idiomatic: Then build eight camps in succession up to the great dike.

sentences.zh: 築甬道輸河北之粟，以餉城中。

translations.literal: I will build a covered way to move grain from north of the river and supply the city.
translations.idiomatic: A covered way will bring grain from the north bank to feed the city.

sentences.zh: 賊兵已老，可一戰走也。

translations.literal: The bandit troops are already worn out; one battle can put them to flight.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are exhausted; a single engagement should drive them off.

sentences.zh: 」諸軍皆曰：「善。

translations.literal: " All the armies said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: " The commanders all agreed: "Well said."

sentences.zh: 」乃以兵三千人先渡立營。

translations.literal: " He then sent three thousand men across first to establish a camp.
translations.idiomatic: " He crossed first with three thousand men and pitched camp.

sentences.zh: 賊攻之，戰三晝夜，諸軍無繼者，甬道不就，澤清拔營歸。

translations.literal: The bandits attacked them; they fought three days and nights; no army came up in support; the covered way was not completed; Zeqing withdrew his camp and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels assaulted the bridgehead; after three days and nights with no reinforcements and no covered way finished, Zeqing pulled back.

sentences.zh: 日夜望傳庭出關，不至。

translations.literal: Day and night they looked for Chuanting to march out of the passes; he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: They waited day and night for Chuanting to emerge from the passes, but he never came.

sentences.zh: 賊圖開封者三，士馬損傷多，積憤，誓必拔之。

translations.literal: The bandits had thrice attempted Kaifeng; men and horses had suffered heavy losses; resentment had piled up; they swore they must take it.
translations.idiomatic: Having failed twice before at Kaifeng, with heavy casualties and mounting rage, the rebels swore the city would fall.

sentences.zh: 圍半年，師老糧匱，欲決黃河灌之。

translations.literal: After half a year of siege the army was weary and provisions exhausted; they wished to breach the Yellow River to flood it.
translations.idiomatic: Six months into the siege, with troops spent and grain gone, they planned to break the Yellow River and drown the city.

sentences.zh: 以城中子女貨寶，猶豫不決。

translations.literal: Because of the women, children, goods, and treasures in the city, they hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The city's people and wealth gave them pause, and they could not bring themselves to act.

sentences.zh: 聞秦師已東，恐諸鎮兵夾擊，欲變計。

translations.literal: Hearing that the Qin armies had already moved east, they feared a pincer from the garrison forces and wished to change their plan.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Shaanxi troops were marching east, fearing encirclement by allied garrisons, they sought another course.

sentences.zh: 會有獻計於巡按御史嚴雲京者，請決河以灌賊。

translations.literal: It happened that someone offered a plan to touring censor Yan Yunjing, asking to breach the river to flood the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Someone then proposed to touring censor Yan Yunjing that the river be opened to flood the rebels.

sentences.zh: 雲京語名衡、澍，名衡、澍以為然。

translations.literal: Yunjing told Mingheng and Shu; Mingheng and Shu thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjing spoke with Mingheng and Huang Shu, and both agreed.

sentences.zh: 周王恭枵募民築羊馬墻，堅厚如高岸。

translations.literal: Prince Gongxiao of Zhou recruited the people to build sheep-and-horse walls, solid and thick as high banks.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhou, Gongxiao, mobilized civilians to raise parapets as thick and firm as river levees.

sentences.zh: 賊營直傅大堤，河決賊可盡，城中無虞。

translations.literal: The bandit camps pressed directly against the great dike; if the river were breached the bandits could be wiped out, and the city would be unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel camps hugged the main embankment; a breach would sweep them away while the city stood safe.

sentences.zh: 我方鑿朱家寨口，賊知，移營高阜，艨艟巨筏以待，而驅掠民夫數萬反決馬家口以灌城。

translations.literal: Our side was digging open the Zhujiazhai breach; the bandits learned of it, moved camp to high ground, and with warships and great rafts waited in readiness, while driving tens of thousands of impressed laborers to breach Majiakou instead and flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: While defenders opened Zhujiazhai, the rebels shifted to high ground with warships and rafts at the ready, then forced tens of thousands of civilians to cut Majiakou and turn the flood against the city.

sentences.zh: 九月癸未望，夜半，二口並決。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month, at midnight, both breaches opened at once.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on the full moon of the ninth month, both cuts gave way together.

sentences.zh: 天大雨連旬，黃流驟漲，聲聞百里。

translations.literal: Heaven sent heavy rain for ten days running; the yellow torrent surged suddenly; the sound was heard a hundred li away.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell for ten days straight; the Yellow River rose in a roaring flood audible a hundred li off.

sentences.zh: 丁夫荷鍤者，隨堤漂沒十數萬，賊亦沈萬人。

translations.literal: Laborers bearing spades, swept from the dike and drowned, numbered in the hundreds of thousands; the bandits also sank ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of thousands of diggers were swept from the embankment and drowned; ten thousand rebels went under as well.

sentences.zh: 河入自北門，貫東南門以出，流入於渦水。

translations.literal: The river entered through the north gate, passed through the southeast gate, and flowed out into the Wo River.
translations.idiomatic: Water poured in the north gate, cut through the southeast gate, and ran off into the Wo River.

sentences.zh: 名衡、永福乘小舟至城頭，周王率其宮眷及寧鄉諸郡王避水棲城樓，坐雨絕食者七日。

translations.literal: Mingheng and Yongfu took small boats to the top of the wall; the Prince of Zhou led his palace women and the princes of Ningxiang and other commanderies to escape the water by sheltering in the gate towers; they sat in the rain without food for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Mingheng and Yongfu reached the walltop by boat while the Prince of Zhou, his consorts, and the Ningxiang princes took refuge in the gate towers, seven days without food in the driving rain.

sentences.zh: 王燮以舟迎王，王從城上泛舟出，名衡等皆出。

translations.literal: Wang Xie came with boats to receive the prince; the prince floated out from atop the wall; Mingheng and the others all came out as well.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xie sent boats for the prince, who floated out over the ramparts; Mingheng and his colleagues escaped with him.

sentences.zh: 茂灼、士奇久餓不能起，並溺死。

translations.literal: Maozhuo and Shiji, long starved, could not rise; both drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhuo and Shiji, too weak from hunger to stand, drowned together.

sentences.zh: 賊浮艦入城，遺民俱盡，拔營而西。

translations.literal: The bandits floated warships into the city; the surviving people were all gone; they broke camp and marched west.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels sailed into the drowned city; the last inhabitants perished; then they broke camp and withdrew west.

sentences.zh: 城初圍時百萬戶，後饑疫死者十二三。

translations.literal: When the city was first besieged it had a million households; afterward hunger and pestilence killed one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng had held a million households at the siege's start; famine and plague later killed perhaps a tenth of them.

sentences.zh: 汴梁佳麗甲中州，群盜心艷之，至是盡沒於水。

translations.literal: Bianliang's beauties were foremost in the Central Plain; the bandits had coveted them; at this they were all lost in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng's celebrated women had been the envy of every rebel camp; now they vanished beneath the flood.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，痛悼。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stricken with grief on hearing the news.

sentences.zh: 猶念諸臣拒守勞，命敘功。

translations.literal: Still mindful of the ministers' labor in holding the defense, he ordered their merits recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering how hard his defenders had fought, he ordered their service rewarded.

sentences.zh: 加名衡兵部右侍郎，名衡辭以疾。

translations.literal: Mingheng was promoted to Vice Minister of War; Mingheng declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Mingheng was made Vice Minister of War but pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 即擢王漢右僉都御史，代名衡巡撫河南。

translations.literal: Wang Han was at once elevated to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief to replace Mingheng as grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han was promoted Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and sent to replace Mingheng as Henan grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 名衡歸，未幾，大清兵破沂州，名衡夫婦殉難。

translations.literal: Mingheng returned home; before long the Great Qing army took Yizhou, and Mingheng and his wife died martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: Mingheng went home; soon after, Qing forces captured Yizhou, and he and his wife died defending it.

sentences.zh: 王漢，字子房，掖縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Han, styled Zifang, was a native of Ye County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han, styled Zifang, came from Ye County.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年進士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in Chongzhen 10.

sentences.zh: 除高平知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He became magistrate of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 調河內，擒巨寇天壇山劉二。

translations.literal: Transferred to Henei, he captured the great bandit Liu Er of Tiantan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At Henei he captured the bandit chieftain Liu Er of Tiantan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 又乘雪夜破妖僧智善。

translations.literal: Again, on a snowy night he broke the sorcerer-monk Zhishan.
translations.idiomatic: He also routed the sorcerer-monk Zhishan in a night attack through snow.

sentences.zh: 夜半渡河，破賊楊六郎。

translations.literal: At midnight he crossed the river and broke the bandit Yang Liulang.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the river at midnight, he smashed Yang Liulang's band.

sentences.zh: 李自成圍開封，漢然火金龍口柳林為疑兵，遣死士入賊中，聲言：「諸鎮兵來援，各數十萬至矣。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng besieged Kaifeng, Han set fires at the Jinlongkou willow grove as a feint and sent death-defying men into the rebel ranks, proclaiming: "Relief armies from the garrisons have arrived, each numbering several hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: During Li Zicheng's siege of Kaifeng, Han lit decoy fires at Jinlongkou and slipped agents into rebel lines to spread word that garrison relief—hundreds of thousands strong—had arrived.

sentences.zh: 」賊聞則驚走。

translations.literal: " When the bandits heard it they fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels panicked and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 漢為人負氣愛士。

translations.literal: Han was by nature proud and fond of nurturing men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Han was proud-spirited and devoted to men of ability.

sentences.zh: 人有一長，嗟嘆之不容口。

translations.literal: If a man had a single strength, he would praise it without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He never tired of praising even one small gift in a man.

sentences.zh: 僚屬紳士陳民疾苦，或言己過，則瞿然下拜。

translations.literal: When subordinates or gentry reported the people's hardships or spoke of his own faults, he would start and bow low.
translations.idiomatic: If an aide or local notable told him of public suffering—or of his own failings—he would bow in sudden humility.

sentences.zh: 用兵士卒同甘苦，人樂為之死。

translations.literal: In campaigning he shared hardship with the soldiers; men were glad to die for him.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he ate and marched with his troops, and they willingly died for him.

sentences.zh: 好用間，賊中虛實莫不知。

translations.literal: He was skilled in using spies; nothing of the bandits' strength or weakness escaped him.
translations.idiomatic: A master of espionage, he always knew the rebels' true condition.

sentences.zh: 攻天壇山賊，山陡絕，登者挽以布。

translations.literal: When he attacked the Tiantan Mountain bandits, the mountain was steep and sheer; climbers were hauled up by cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Assaulting Tiantan Mountain, where the cliffs were sheer, his men were pulled up on cloth ropes.

sentences.zh: 漢持刀直上，人服其勇。

translations.literal: Han took a blade and climbed straight up; men admired his courage.
translations.idiomatic: Han climbed sword in hand; all marveled at his daring.

sentences.zh: 時賊氛日熾，帝每臨朝而嘆漢前後破賊功，降旨優敘。

translations.literal: As bandit troubles grew daily fiercer, whenever the emperor held court he would sigh over Han's successive victories and issue edicts of special reward.
translations.idiomatic: With rebellion spreading, the emperor often sighed over Han's victories and sent edicts of special commendation.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，以減俸行取入都，與蘇京、王燮同召對，稱旨。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year, his salary reduced, he was summoned to the capital by special selection; with Su Jing and Wang Xie he was called to audience and pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 15, summoned to court despite a pay cut, he and Su Jing and Wang Xie met the emperor and won his approval.

sentences.zh: 命三臣皆以試御史監軍。

translations.literal: The three ministers were all ordered to serve as provisional censors supervising armies.
translations.idiomatic: All three were appointed provisional censor-supervisors of the field armies.

sentences.zh: 漢監平賊鎮標楚、蜀軍，與督臣侯恂南援汴。

translations.literal: Han supervised the Chu and Shu troops of the Pacification Army and marched south with Grand Coordinator Hou Xun to relieve Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Han took command of Pacification Army Chu and Shu units and marched south with Hou Xun to save Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 時兵部奏援剿兵十萬，十之四以屬京、燮，屬漢以其六。

translations.literal: At the time the Ministry of War reported one hundred thousand relief and suppression troops; four-tenths were assigned to Jing and Xie, and six-tenths to Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War listed a hundred thousand relief troops; forty percent went to Su Jing and Wang Xie, sixty to Han.

sentences.zh: 漢所監凡五萬九千，然大半已潰散，兵部空名使之。

translations.literal: The troops Han supervised totaled fifty-nine thousand, but more than half had already scattered; the Ministry of War gave him empty names.
translations.idiomatic: Han nominally commanded fifty-nine thousand men, but most had already fled; the ministry had only titles to offer.

sentences.zh: 漢乃請自立標營兵千人，騎二百，報可。

translations.literal: Han then requested permission to raise his own standard camp of a thousand infantry and two hundred cavalry; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to form a thousand-man infantry and two-hundred-horse cavalry command of his own; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃簡保營兵百余人，募邯鄲、鉅鹿壯士三百人，又取故治河內所練義兵及修武、濟源素從征剿者五百人，及親故子弟，合千人。

translations.literal: He then selected more than a hundred Pacification Army troops, recruited three hundred stalwarts from Handan and Julu, also took five hundred militia he had trained while governing Henei and men from Xiuwu and Jiyuan who had long followed the campaigns, together with kinsmen and friends' sons—altogether a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: From Pacification Army veterans, Handan and Julu recruits, his old Henei militia, campaign-hardened men from Xiuwu and Jiyuan, and sons of kin and friends, he assembled a thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 八月朔夜半，襲賊範家灘，斬一紅甲賊目。

translations.literal: At midnight on the first day of the eighth month he raided Fanjiatan and beheaded one red-armored bandit chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: On the first night of the eighth month he struck Fanjiatan and killed a red-armored rebel officer.

sentences.zh: 檄諸將合剿。

translations.literal: He issued orders to the generals for a combined suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He called on all generals to join in a joint attack.

sentences.zh: 自走襄陽，督左良玉兵救汴。

translations.literal: He himself went to Xiangyang and directed Zuo Liangyu's troops to save Bian.
translations.idiomatic: He raced to Xiangyang to hurry Zuo Liangyu's army toward Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 至潼關，有詔漢巡按河南。

translations.literal: When he reached Tong Pass, an edict made Han touring censor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass he received orders appointing him Henan touring censor.

sentences.zh: 時賊灌開封，漢聞，趣諸將自柳園夜半渡河，伏兵西岸。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits were flooding Kaifeng; on hearing it, Han urged the generals to cross the river from Liuyuan at midnight and lay ambush on the west bank.
translations.idiomatic: When Kaifeng was inundated, Han rushed the generals to cross from Liuyuan at midnight and hide on the west bank.

sentences.zh: 檄卜從善等夾攻之，斬首九十余級，遂入汴，大張旗鼓為疑兵。

translations.literal: He ordered Bu Congshan and others to attack from both sides; more than ninety heads were taken; then he entered Bian and raised banners and drums as a feint.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Congshan and others struck from both flanks, taking ninety heads; Han then entered Kaifeng and beat drums and flags as a deception.

sentences.zh: 追賊至朱仙鎮，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Pursuing the bandits to Zhuxian Town, he won victory in successive battles.
translations.idiomatic: He chased the rebels to Zhuxian Town and won a string of engagements.

sentences.zh: 巡撫高名衡謝病，即擢漢右僉都御史代之。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Gao Mingheng pleaded illness; Han was at once promoted Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Mingheng stepped down ill, Han was promoted Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 漢乃廣間諜，收土豪，議屯田，謀所以圖賊。

translations.literal: Han then expanded his spy network, rallied local strongmen, discussed garrison farming, and plotted how to destroy the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He widened his intelligence, rallied local power-holders, planned garrison agriculture, and schemed against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 無何，劉超反永城。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Chao rebelled at Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Chao rose in revolt at Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 超，永城人，跛而狡，為貴州總兵，坐罪免。

translations.literal: Chao was a native of Yongcheng, lame and cunning; he had been regional commander of Guizhou and was dismissed for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: A lame, wily Yongcheng man, Liu Chao had served as Guizhou regional commander until dismissed for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 上疏言兵計，陳新甲用為河南總兵。

translations.literal: He memorialized on military plans; Chen Xin'a employed him as Henan regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted plans for the armies, and Chen Xin'a made him Henan regional commander.

sentences.zh: 以私怨殺其鄉官御史魏景琦一家三十余人，懼罪，遂據城反。

translations.literal: Out of private hatred he killed more than thirty members of the family of his hometown censor Wei Jingqi; fearing punishment, he then seized the city and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered more than thirty kin of local censor Wei Jingqi in a private vendetta, then rebelled and held the city for fear of retribution.

sentences.zh: 漢上疏請討，語泄，超得為備。

translations.literal: Han memorialized asking to suppress him; the plan leaked and Chao was able to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Han requested permission to attack, but word leaked and Chao made ready.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，漢入永城，聲言招撫，為賊所殺。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Han entered Yongcheng, claiming he came to offer amnesty; the bandits killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The next first month he entered Yongcheng under the guise of amnesty and was murdered by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 參將陳治邦、遊擊連光耀父子皆戰死。

translations.literal: Assistant Regional Commander Chen Zhibang and Mobile Corps Commander Lian Guangyao, father and son, all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhibang and the father-and-son team Lian Guangyao fell fighting.

sentences.zh: 遊擊馬魁負漢屍以出，面如生。

translations.literal: Mobile Corps Commander Ma Kui carried Han's body out; his face was as in life.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Kui bore Han's corpse from the field; his face looked untouched by death.

sentences.zh: 詔贈兵部尚書，蔭錦衣世百戶，建祠致祭。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Minister of War, ennobled a hereditary hundred-household Guard officer, and ordered a shrine built for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Minister of War, granted hereditary Guard rank to a hundred households, and ordered a memorial shrine.

sentences.zh: 既而超伏誅，傳首九邊。

translations.literal: Before long Chao was executed; his head was sent to the nine border regions.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was soon caught and executed; his head was displayed on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 徐汧，字九一，長洲人。

translations.literal: Xu Qian, styled Jiuyi, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qian, styled Jiuyi, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 生未期而孤。

translations.literal: He was orphaned before he was one year old.
translations.idiomatic: His father died before his first birthday.

sentences.zh: 稍長砥行，有時名，與同里楊廷樞相友善。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat he polished his conduct; he had a reputation of the age and was close friends with his townsman Yang Tingshu.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he cultivated his character, won local renown, and befriended Yang Tingshu of the same district.

sentences.zh: 廷樞，復社諸生所稱維鬥先生者也。

translations.literal: Tingshu was the Fushe student whom all called Master Weidou.
translations.idiomatic: Tingshu was the Fushe scholar known everywhere as Master Weidou.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年，魏大中被逮過薊州，汧貸金資其行。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi, when Wei Dazhong was arrested and passed through Jizhou, Qian lent him gold for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 5, when Wei Dazhong was seized and marched through Jizhou, Qian lent him travel money.

sentences.zh: 周順昌被逮，緹騎橫索錢，汧與廷樞斂財經理之。

translations.literal: When Zhou Shunchang was arrested, the arresting riders extorted money without restraint; Qian and Tingshu gathered funds and managed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Shunchang was taken, the bailiffs demanded bribes; Qian and Tingshu raised money to see him through.

sentences.zh: 當是時，汧、廷樞名聞天下。

translations.literal: At that time the names of Qian and Tingshu were known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: By then Qian and Tingshu were famous across the empire.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，汧成進士，改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, Qian passed the metropolitan examination, became a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin, and was made a reviser.

sentences.zh: 三年，廷樞舉應天鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the third year Tingshu placed first in the Jiangnan provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Tingshu topped the Jiangnan provincial exams.

sentences.zh: 中允黃道周以救錢龍錫貶官。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Huang Daozhou was demoted for pleading for Qian Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou was reduced in rank for defending Qian Longxi.

sentences.zh: 倪元璐，道周同年生，請以己代謫，帝不允。

translations.literal: Ni Yuanlu, Daozhou's fellow graduate, asked to take the demotion in his stead; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Yuanlu, Daozhou's classmate, offered to accept the punishment himself; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 汧上疏頌道周、元璐賢，且自請罷黜，帝詰責汧。

translations.literal: Qian memorialized praising the worth of Daozhou and Yuanlu, and also asked to be dismissed himself; the emperor rebuked Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Qian praised Daozhou and Yuanlu in a memorial and asked to be removed from office; the emperor scolded him.

sentences.zh: 汧曰：「推賢讓能，藎臣所務；

translations.literal: Qian said: "Promoting the worthy and yielding to the able is the loyal minister's duty;
translations.idiomatic: Qian replied: "To advance the worthy and yield to the able is what a loyal minister owes the throne;

sentences.zh: 難進易退，儒者之風。

translations.literal: hard to advance and easy to withdraw is the scholar's way.
translations.idiomatic: to enter reluctantly and withdraw readily is the scholar's way.

sentences.zh: 間者陛下委任之意希註外廷，防察之權輒逮閽寺，默窺聖意，疑貳漸萌。

translations.literal: Of late Your Majesty's intent in conferring appointments rarely extends to the outer court, while the power of surveillance and inspection constantly reaches the inner eunuchs; silently reading the imperial mind, doubts and divisions have gradually taken root.
translations.idiomatic: Lately appointments rarely reach the outer court, yet surveillance powers keep falling to the eunuchs; reading the throne's mood, men have begun to doubt and divide.

sentences.zh: 萬一士風日賤，宸向日移，明盛之時為憂方大。

translations.literal: If the spirit of the scholar-official class should daily grow base and the imperial countenance should daily shift, the worry for the Ming at its height would be very great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Should official morale sink and the emperor's favor swing day by day, the dynasty's golden age would be in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not hear him.

sentences.zh: 汧尋乞假歸。

translations.literal: Qian soon asked leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Qian soon took leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 還朝，遷右庶子，充日講官。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was transferred to Right Sub-Reader and appointed daily lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he became Right Sub-Reader and a daily lecturer to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十四年奉使益王府，便道還家。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he went on mission to the Prince of Yi's domain and returned home by the direct route.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he served as envoy to the Prince of Yi and visited home on the way.

sentences.zh: 當是時，復社諸生氣甚盛，汧與廷樞、顧杲、華允誠等往復尤契。

translations.literal: At that time the spirit of the Fushe students ran very high; Qian was especially close in correspondence with Tingshu, Gu Gao, Hua Yuncheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Fushe's scholars were at their zenith; Qian corresponded most closely with Tingshu, Gu Gao, Hua Yuncheng, and their circle.

sentences.zh: 居久之，京師陷。

translations.literal: After some time the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Beijing fell.

sentences.zh: 福王召汧為少詹事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu summoned Qian as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu called Qian to serve as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 汧以國破君亡，臣子不當叨位，且痛宗社之喪亡，由朋黨相傾，移書當事，勸以力破異同之見。

translations.literal: Qian held that with the state broken and the ruler dead a subject should not cling to office; moreover he grieved that the altars had perished through partisan strife, and wrote to those in power urging them to break down divisions of opinion by force of will.
translations.idiomatic: Believing no loyal subject should take rank after the realm's fall, and grieving that faction had destroyed the dynasty, he wrote the court urging an end to partisan rancor.

sentences.zh: 既就職，陳時政七事，忄卷忄卷以化恩仇、去偏黨為言。

translations.literal: Once he took office he set forth seven points on current policy, earnestly urging reconciliation of old enmities and removal of partisan cliques.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he offered seven reforms, earnestly pleading that grudges be healed and factions set aside.

sentences.zh: 而安遠侯柳祚昌疏攻汧，謂：「朝服謁潞王於京口，自恃東林巨魁，與復社楊廷樞、顧杲諸奸狼狽相倚。

translations.literal: But Marquis Liu Zuochang of Anyuan attacked Qian in a memorial, saying: "Dressed in court robes he paid court to the Prince of Lu at Jingkou, relying on himself as a Donglin chieftain and in collusion with the Fushe men Yang Tingshu, Gu Gao, and other villains."
