translations.idiomatic: Marquis Liu Zuochang of Anyuan then impeached him, charging that Qian—in court dress—had visited the Prince of Lu at Jingkou, posing as a Donglin boss in league with Fushe's Yang Tingshu, Gu Gao, and other ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 陛下定鼎金陵，彼為《討金陵檄》，所雲『中原逐鹿，南國指馬』是何語？

translations.literal: Your Majesty has fixed the capital at Jinling; they drafted a Jinling proclamation—what do they mean by the words 'the Central Plain contends for the deer, the southern realm points at the horse'?
translations.idiomatic: With the throne established at Jinling, they circulated a denunciation asking what was meant by 'contending for the realm in the north while marking out the south's steed.'

sentences.zh: 乞置汧於理，除廷樞、杲名，其余徒黨，容臣次第糾彈。

translations.literal: I beg that Qian be handed over to the law, that Tingshu and Gao be struck from the rolls, and that the remaining partisans be impeached by degrees at your servant's discretion.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded Qian be prosecuted, Tingshu and Gao removed from office, and the rest of the clique impeached one by one.

sentences.zh: 」時國事方棘，事亦竟寢。

translations.literal: " At the time state affairs were urgently pressed; the matter in the end came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " But with the realm in crisis, the accusation was quietly dropped.

sentences.zh: 汧移疾歸。

translations.literal: Qian resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Qian pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 明年，南京失守，蘇、常相繼下。

translations.literal: The next year Nanjing fell; Suzhou and Changzhou fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Nanjing fell, then Suzhou and Changzhou in turn.

sentences.zh: 汧慨然太息，作書戒二子，投虎丘新塘橋下死。

translations.literal: Qian sighed deeply, wrote letters admonishing his two sons, and drowned himself beneath the new Tang Bridge at Tiger Hill.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed in grief, wrote final letters to his sons, and drowned himself at the New Tang Bridge below Tiger Hill.

sentences.zh: 郡人赴哭者數千人。

translations.literal: Several thousand people of the commandery came to weep for him.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands from the prefecture came to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 時又有一人儒冠藍衫而來，躍虎丘劍池中，土人憐而葬之，卒不知何人也。

translations.literal: At the same time another man came in scholar's cap and blue robe and leaped into the Sword Pool at Tiger Hill; the locals pitied him and buried him, yet in the end none knew who he was.
translations.idiomatic: About then another man in cap and gown threw himself into Tiger Hill's Sword Pool; villagers buried him in pity, never learning his name.

sentences.zh: 於是廷樞聞變，走避之鄧尉山中。

translations.literal: Thereupon, when Tingshu heard the calamity, he fled for refuge in the Dengwei Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingshu heard the news, he fled into the Dengwei hills.

sentences.zh: 久之，四方弄兵者群起，廷樞負重名，鹹指目廷樞。

translations.literal: After a long while, as armed bands rose everywhere, Tingshu bore a great name and all eyes turned toward Tingshu.
translations.idiomatic: As warlords sprang up across the land, Tingshu's fame made him the man everyone watched.

sentences.zh: 當事者執廷樞，好言慰之，廷樞嫚罵不已，殺之蘆墟泗洲寺。

translations.literal: Those in power seized Tingshu and spoke soothing words to him; Tingshu reviled them without cease and was killed at Luzhu Sizhou Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities arrested Tingshu, tried to placate him, and when he cursed them without stopping, executed him at Luzhu Sizhou Temple.

sentences.zh: 首已墮，聲從項中出，益厲。

translations.literal: His head had already fallen, yet a voice came from his neck, fiercer than before.
translations.idiomatic: Even after decapitation a voice rose from his neck, louder and fiercer than before.

sentences.zh: 門人迮紹原購其屍葬焉。

translations.literal: His disciple Zuo Shaoyuan purchased his corpse and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: His student Zuo Shaoyuan bought his body and gave it burial.

sentences.zh: 汧子枋，字昭法，舉十五年鄉試。

translations.literal: Qian's son Fang, styled Zhaofa, passed the provincial examination in the fifteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's son Fang, styled Zhaofa, passed the provincial exam in year 15.

sentences.zh: 枋依隱，有高行雲。

translations.literal: Fang lived in reclusion and had a lofty reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Fang withdrew from public life and was honored for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 鹿善繼，字伯順，定興人。

translations.literal: Lu Shanji, styled Boshun, was a native of Dingxing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shanji, styled Boshun, came from Dingxing.

sentences.zh: 祖久征，萬歷中進士，授息縣知縣。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jiuzheng, a jinshi in the Wanli reign, was appointed magistrate of Xi County.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiuzheng, a Wanli-era jinshi, served as magistrate of Xi County.

sentences.zh: 時詔天下度田，各署上中下壤，息獨以下田報，曰：「度田以紓民，乃病民乎！

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered land throughout the realm surveyed and each district to report upper, middle, and lower grades of soil; Xi alone reported lower fields, saying: "Land survey was meant to ease the people—does it instead afflict them?"
translations.idiomatic: When the throne ordered a national land survey graded by soil quality, Xi County alone reported all fields as lower grade, asking: "Was the survey meant to relieve the people or to harm them?"

sentences.zh: 」調襄垣，擢御史，以言事謫澤州判官，遷滎澤知縣，未任而卒。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Xiangyuan, promoted to censor, demoted to magistrate of Zecheng for memorializing, then moved to magistrate of Yingze; he died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: " Transferred to Xiangyuan and made censor, he was banished to Zecheng for speaking out, then appointed to Yingze, but died before he could serve.

sentences.zh: 父正，苦節自礪。

translations.literal: His father Zheng cultivated stern integrity and disciplined himself.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng lived in austere self-discipline.

sentences.zh: 縣令某欲見之，方糞田，投鍤而往。

translations.literal: When a certain magistrate wished to see him, he was manuring a field; he threw down his spade and went.
translations.idiomatic: A magistrate once came to call while he was spreading manure; he dropped his spade and went to meet him.

sentences.zh: 急人之難，傾其家不惜，遠近稱鹿太公。

translations.literal: Urgent to help others in distress, he would empty his house without stint; near and far called him Old Master Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He would ruin his household to aid the distressed; neighbors far and near called him Old Master Lu.

sentences.zh: 善繼端方謹愨。

translations.literal: Shanji was upright, correct, and reverently cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Shanji was upright, careful, and scrupulous.

sentences.zh: 由萬歷四十一年進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: Having passed the metropolitan examination in the forty-first year of Wanli, he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: A Wanli 41 jinshi, he entered the Ministry of Revenue as a secretary.

sentences.zh: 內艱除，起故官。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left office; on mourning's end he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for his mother's mourning and returned afterward to the same post.

sentences.zh: 遼左餉中絕，廷臣數請發帑，不報。

translations.literal: Funds for the eastern Liaodong frontier were cut off; court ministers repeatedly asked that the treasury be opened; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong pay dried up; ministers repeatedly begged for treasury funds and received no answer.

sentences.zh: 會廣東進金花銀，善繼稽舊制，金花貯庫，備各邊應用。

translations.literal: When Guangdong sent tribute silver, Shanji checked the old regulations: tribute silver was stored in the treasury for use on the various frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong delivered tribute silver, Shanji cited precedent that such silver belonged in the treasury for frontier use.

sentences.zh: 乃奏記尚書李汝華曰：「與其請不發之帑，何如留未進之金？

translations.literal: He then wrote to Minister Li Ruhua, saying: "Rather than beg for funds that will not be released, why not retain silver not yet forwarded?"
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Minister Li Ruhua: "Better to hold back silver not yet forwarded than to plead for funds the throne will not release."

sentences.zh: 」汝華然之。

translations.literal: " Ruhua agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Ruhua agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪善繼俸一年，趣補進。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, stripped Shanji of a year's salary, and ordered the silver forwarded at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, docked Shanji a year's pay, and demanded immediate delivery of the silver.

sentences.zh: 善繼持不可，以死爭。

translations.literal: Shanji held that it could not be done and contested to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Shanji refused and fought the order as if his life depended on it.

sentences.zh: 乃奪汝華俸二月，降善繼一級，調外。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ruhua's salary was taken for two months and Shanji was demoted one rank and transferred outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ruhua lost two months' salary; Shanji was demoted and sent out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 汝華懼，卒補銀進。

translations.literal: Ruhua feared, and in the end forwarded the silver.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Li Ruhua finally sent the silver in.

sentences.zh: 泰昌改元，復原官，典新餉。

translations.literal: When Taichang's reign began, Shanji was restored to his former post and put in charge of new frontier pay.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Taichang emperor he was restored and put in charge of new frontier funds.

sentences.zh: 連疏請帑百萬，不報。

translations.literal: He memorialized repeatedly asking for a million from the treasury; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked for a million taels from the treasury and was ignored.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，遼陽陷，以才改兵部職方主事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, when Liaoyang fell, because of his talent he was made a secretary in the Bureau of Operations of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 1, after Liaoyang fell, his ability won him a post in the Ministry of War's Bureau of Operations.

sentences.zh: 大學士孫承宗理兵部事，推心任之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong handled War Ministry affairs and entrusted him with his whole heart.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong ran the War Ministry and gave Shanji his full trust.

sentences.zh: 及閱視關門，以善繼從。

translations.literal: When he inspected the passes and gates, he took Shanji with him.
translations.idiomatic: On inspection tours of the frontier passes he kept Shanji at his side.

sentences.zh: 出督師，復表為贊畫。

translations.literal: When he went out as supreme commander, he again recommended Shanji as strategic planner.
translations.idiomatic: As supreme commander he again named Shanji his strategic planner.

sentences.zh: 布衣羸馬，出入亭障間，延見將卒相勞苦，拓地四百里，收復城堡數十，承宗倚之若左右手。

translations.literal: In plain clothes on a lean horse he went in and out among the fortifications; he received generals and soldiers and comforted them in their hardship; he opened four hundred li of land and recovered several dozen fortresses; Chengzong relied on him as on right hand and left.
translations.idiomatic: Clad plainly on a thin horse he moved among the defenses, comforted officers and men, reclaimed four hundred li of territory and dozens of forts; Chengzong leaned on him like a second self.

sentences.zh: 在關四年，累進員外郎、郎中。

translations.literal: He spent four years at the passes, rising in succession to vice director and director.
translations.idiomatic: Four years on the frontier brought him promotion to vice director and then director.

sentences.zh: 承宗謝事，善繼亦告歸。

translations.literal: When Chengzong retired, Shanji also asked to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong stepped down, Shanji sought leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 先是，楊、左之獄起，魏大中子學洢、左光鬥弟光明，先後投鹿太公家。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the cases of Yang and Zuo arose, Wei Dazhong's son Xueyi and Zuo Guangdou's brother Guangming successively fled to Old Master Lu's house.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Yang–Zuo persecutions, Wei Dazhong's son Xueyi and Zuo Guangdou's brother Guangming both took refuge with Old Master Lu.

sentences.zh: 太公客之，與所善義士容城舉人孫奇逢謀，持書走關門，告其難於承宗。

translations.literal: The Old Master harbored them and, with the righteous gentleman and Rongcheng graduate Sun Qifeng whom he favored, took letters through the passes to tell Chengzong of their peril.
translations.idiomatic: He sheltered them and, with his friend the Rongcheng scholar Sun Qifeng, sent word through the passes to Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 承宗、善繼謀借巡視薊門，請入覲。

translations.literal: Chengzong and Shanji planned, under the pretext of inspecting Jizhou, to request an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong and Shanji planned to enter the capital under cover of inspecting Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 奄黨大嘩，謂閣部將提兵清君側，嚴旨阻之。

translations.literal: The eunuch faction raised a great outcry, saying the Grand Secretariat would march troops to purge the court; stern edicts blocked them.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch partisans cried that the Grand Secretariat meant to march on the capital; stern edicts stopped them.

sentences.zh: 獄益急，五日一追贓，搒掠甚酷。

translations.literal: The cases grew more urgent; every five days restitution was demanded; beating and torture were very cruel.
translations.idiomatic: The prosecutions intensified—restitution demanded every five days amid savage torture.

sentences.zh: 太公急募得數百金輸之，而兩人者則皆已斃矣。

translations.literal: The Old Master urgently raised several hundred taels of silver and sent it in, yet both men had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Old Master Lu frantically raised hundreds of taels in ransom, but both men were already dead.

sentences.zh: 至是，善繼歸，而周順昌之獄又起。

translations.literal: By then Shanji had returned, and Zhou Shunchang's case arose again.
translations.idiomatic: Shanji was home when the persecution of Zhou Shunchang began anew.

sentences.zh: 順昌，善繼同年生，善繼又為募得數百金，金入而順昌又斃。

translations.literal: Shunchang was Shanji's fellow graduate; Shanji again raised several hundred taels for him; the silver arrived and Shunchang was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Shunchang, Shanji's classmate, received the same help—but the silver came too late.

sentences.zh: 奄黨居近善繼家，難家子弟仆從相望於道。

translations.literal: Eunuch partisans lived near Shanji's home; the sons and servants of persecuted families lined the road one after another.
translations.idiomatic: With eunuch allies nearby, the roads around his home filled with the kin and servants of the accused.

sentences.zh: 太公曰：「吾不懼也。

translations.literal: The Old Master said: "I am not afraid."
translations.idiomatic: Old Master Lu said: "I do not fear them."

sentences.zh: 」崇禎元年，逆榼既誅，善繼起尚寶卿，遷太常少卿，管光祿丞事，再請歸。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Chongzhen, after the rebellious eunuchs were executed, Shanji was recalled as Court of Imperial Sacrifices minister, transferred to Vice Minister of Rites in charge of the Directorate of Imperial Banquets, and twice asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: " In Chongzhen 1, after the eunuch tyrants were killed, Shanji returned as Court of Imperial Sacrifices minister, became Vice Minister of Rites overseeing the Banquets Directorate, and twice asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，大清兵攻定興。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year the Great Qing army attacked Dingxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 9 Qing forces attacked Dingxing.

sentences.zh: 善繼家在江村，白太公請入捍城，太公許之。

translations.literal: Shanji's home was at Jiang Village; he told the Old Master he wished to enter the city to defend it; the Old Master consented.
translations.idiomatic: Living at Jiang Village, he asked Old Master Lu's leave to join the city's defense; the old man agreed.

sentences.zh: 與裏居知州薛一鶚等共守。

translations.literal: Together with the retired prefect of the district, Xue Yie, and others, he held the defense.
translations.idiomatic: He defended the city alongside the local retired prefect Xue Yie and others.

sentences.zh: 守六日而城破，善繼死。

translations.literal: After six days of defense the city fell; Shanji died.
translations.idiomatic: Six days into the siege the wall gave way; Shanji was killed.

sentences.zh: 家人奔告太公，太公曰：「嗟乎，吾兒素以身許國，今果死，吾復何憾！

translations.literal: His family ran to tell the Old Master; the Old Master said: "Alas, my son has long pledged his body to the state; now he has indeed died—what regret can I have!"
translations.idiomatic: When his family brought word, Old Master Lu said: "My son long ago gave his life to the realm; now he has paid—what more could I ask?"

sentences.zh: 」事聞，贈善繼大理卿，謚忠節，敕有司建祠。

translations.literal: " When the matter was reported, Shanji was posthumously made Grand Court President, given the posthumous title Zhongjie, and ordered a shrine built by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: " The court posthumously made him Grand Court President, styled him Loyal and Steadfast, and ordered an official shrine.

sentences.zh: 子化麟，舉天啟元年鄉試第一，伏闕訟父忠。

translations.literal: His son Hualin placed first in the provincial examination in the first year of Tianqi and prostrated himself at the palace gate to plead his father's loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hualin topped the Tianqi 1 provincial exams and knelt at the palace gate to vindicate his father.

sentences.zh: 逾年亦卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he too died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he too was dead.

sentences.zh: 薛一鶚，字百當，由貢生為黃州通判。

translations.literal: Xue Yie, styled Baidang, entered office through the tribute-student route as vice prefect of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yie, styled Baidang, became Huangzhou vice prefect by the tribute-student path.

sentences.zh: 荊王姬誣他姬鴆世子，一鶚白其誣。

translations.literal: A consort of the Prince of Jing falsely accused another consort of poisoning the heir; Yie cleared the false charge.
translations.idiomatic: When a Jing prince's consort falsely accused a rival of poisoning the heir, Yie exposed the lie.

sentences.zh: 奄人傳太妃命，欲竟其獄，卒直之。

translations.literal: A eunuch conveyed the Grand Consort's command, wishing to close the case; in the end Yie saw justice done.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch brought the Grand Consort's order to bury the matter; Yie insisted on the truth.

sentences.zh: 遷蘭州知州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 州北有田沒於番，吏派其賦於他戶，後田復歸，為衛卒所據，而民出賦三十年，一鶚核除其害。

translations.literal: North of the prefecture fields had been lost to the tribes; officials assigned their tax burden to other households; later when the fields returned they were seized by garrison soldiers while the people paid tax for thirty years; Yie verified the accounts and removed the injury.
translations.idiomatic: When tribal incursions had swallowed northern fields, officials shifted the tax to others; even after the land returned, garrison troops held it while commoners paid thirty years of levies; Yie audited the rolls and lifted the burden.

sentences.zh: 至是佐善繼城守，遂同死。

translations.literal: At this time he assisted Shanji in holding the city and died together with him.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Shanji in the defense of Dingxing and died at his side.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：士大夫致政裏居，無封疆民社之責，可遜跡自全，非以必死為勇也。

translations.literal: Commentary: When scholar-officials retire to their home districts they bear no charge over frontiers or the people's altars of soil and grain; they may withdraw and preserve themselves—courage is not shown by dying as a matter of course.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: retired officials at home owe no frontier or communal charge; they may withdraw and save themselves—bravery is not measured by courting death.

sentences.zh: 然而慷慨捐軀，冒白刃而不悔，湛宗覆族，君子哀之。

translations.literal: Yet they gave their bodies generously, faced naked blades without regret, and drenched their clans and ancestors in ruin—men of honor mourned them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they gave their lives freely, faced the blade without regret, and brought ruin on kin and clan—worthy men grieved for them.

sentences.zh: 豈非名義所在，有重於生者乎！

translations.literal: Was it not that reputation and duty weighed more than life itself!
translations.idiomatic: Was it not that duty and honor outweighed life itself!

sentences.zh: 氣節凜然，要於自遂其誌。

translations.literal: Their moral bearing was stern and bright; what mattered was fulfilling their own resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Their integrity stood bright; what mattered was to follow their chosen path.

sentences.zh: 其英風義烈，固不可泯沒於宇宙間矣。

translations.literal: Their heroic spirit and righteous fervor surely cannot be erased from the universe.
translations.idiomatic: Their heroic spirit and righteous zeal cannot be erased from the world.
